_comment: The tier map (card 199). What a tool can DO, decided by the product and shipped
with the build, because the protocol cannot say it: both MCP transports pin
revision 2024-11-05, and that revision carries no tool annotations at all —
readOnlyHint and its siblings arrived in 2025-03-26. A server therefore never
rates its own tools here; this file does.
Anything this file does not name resolves to eval-execute and prompts. That
makes a partial section SAFE by construction: a section can only ever narrow
what an allowlist entry approves, never widen it. It also names the cost —
a server that grows a tool produces prompts on the day it updates, and the fix
is an entry in the next release, not a config edit on the user's machine.
bump mapVersion on every content change; the resolved tier and this version
land on every gate audit line.
The built-in tool belt. read_file/list_dir/glob/grep/view_* look and never
touch. web_fetch looks too — what bounds its REACH is the net fence, not its
tier. browse_page is write: it launches a real browser and navigates, which
the tier table rates alongside browser_navigate. run_command and the spawn
tools run code — a child agent's own registry carries run_command, so a
spawn is an eval one indirection away.
The browser_* family (card 201) is rated by what each tool DOES to the page.
browser_read_page, browser_find and browser_read_console look and never touch.
browser_navigate and browser_resize act on the pane; browser_computer bundles a
screenshot (read) with input injection (write), and a tool's tier is its widest
capability, so it is write. browser_eval is eval-execute and deliberately so:
it runs model-authored JavaScript in the PAGE context, holding that origin's
cookies, localStorage and fetch credentials, and it acts with the authority of
whoever is logged in there — against a page that is attacker-influenced input.
A :read ceiling must never approve it. There is no Node-context eval here and
none gets added (card 200, section 6, rule 4).
One section per blessed MCP server, keyed by the CONFIGURED server name —
the middle segment of mcp__<server>__<tool>. A server absent from here rates
none of its tools: every one of them is eval-execute and prompts.

spectro-notes._comment: The in-house notes server (spectro-mcp-notes), measured from its own tools/list.

_comment: Deliberately PARTIAL. Only what card 199 measured is named; every other
playwright tool falls to eval-execute and prompts until a release adds it.
browser_run_code_unsafe is the tool the stress test named: it runs in the
NODE context with the full filesystem, and a name-only wildcard used to
approve it beside the screenshots.
